name: darkreach-05
note: DEPARTURE REPRODUCTION card, R29 follow-up. In R29 the Darkreach flew its first six cards clean at this entry condition - 0 rails, 0.33 deg median terminal error, pitch-effectiveness starvation gone (pEff<0.15 fell 65.4% -> 0.00%) - and then on the 0.5 deg card the roll-to-align channel demanded 55-63 deg of BANK against a 1.3 deg azimuth error, and it departed two cards later at 26.9 g / -87 deg AoA, killing the pilot. Sidecars proved no prior damage, so this is a control-law defect and not battle attrition. This card isolates that: the oblique-05 geometry, the Darkreach alone, at the exact speed it flew in R29. PRIMARY MEASURABLE is the PRECURSOR, not the crash - a 55-63 deg targetBank against a ~1 deg error is a within-segment event and should recur on this geometry whether or not the full departure does. Read targetBank / rollCmd / bWt against azErr; a healthy capture commands NO bank at all below 0.5 deg of azErr (measured 0.0% of samples on 25 fixedwing-v2 captures). Any capture where targetBank exceeds ~10 deg while |azErr| < 2 deg is the defect firing. Departures are expected and are DATA - a truncated capture here is a result, not a failed run. startSpeed is written ABSOLUTE (171 m/s) and STAYS absolute, deliberately: 171 m/s is the condition R29 and R32 actually flew, and reproducing that departure IS the card. startSpeedCorner works correctly since v0.96 (it resolves against the FBW's cornerSpeed, not the AI table's - AIRFRAMES.md trap 6), but it would not be a more portable spelling of this condition, it would be a DIFFERENT one: this airframe's FBW corner is 100 m/s against the AI table's 180, so 0.95x would place it at 95 m/s instead of 171. Do not convert it. NO armToggle on purpose - one card, one test, and this one has to first establish that the precursor reproduces before any lever is swept against it. Tags are shared with oblique-05 by design; compare-runs.py keys on card name and scorecard.py already resolves them, so no tool change. AIRFRAME: Darkreach only - it is the only airframe that has shown this, and at 54 t it is the heavy end where the R28/R29 ranking puts the failure.
